factorRatings.note: The Infatuation rated it 7.5/10, calling the Roman by-the-cut al taglio pizza 'pretty good' with hit-or-miss toppings but singling out the Margherita and wild boar bolognese as standouts; CHS covered its Capitol Hill debut from the Brunton brothers, whose three-day naturally leavened dough anchors a concept built as much around the room and cocktails as the pizza.

The Seattle Times called the original location worth a 'pizza pilgrimage' for its burrata-and-hot-honey pies on a 'crispy, never burned crust' and later crowned it champion of its citywide Pizza Smackdown; the Phinney Ridge location, opened in 2026, is now the flagship producing dough for all locations, and The Infatuation confirms it serves 'the same burrata-dolloped pies.'

The Infatuation scored it 8.8/10, praising 'sturdy-but-light caramelized crusts' and calling the plain Detroit-style pie 'sublime,' alongside inventive slices like a Fishy Caesar; a Seattle pizza-focused newsletter ranked it #3 in its Definitive Seattle Pizza Rankings.

The Infatuation rated it 7.8/10 for its two-day cold-fermented, crackly-crust Roman al taglio slices and diaspora-inspired toppings like Jamaican-curry mushroom and gumbo-style pies; Seattle Refined covered its distinction as Washington's first Black-owned pizzeria, opened October 2024, which redirects tips to a nonprofit funding school garden grants.

The Seattle Times called it home to 'some of the best Neapolitan-style pizza around' in a traditional white-tiled oven; The Infatuation likewise praised its 'bubbly pies drizzled with chile oil' in a cozy, narrow, date-friendly room, and PhinneyWood covered its 2016 opening in Phinney Ridge/Greenwood by brothers Andrew and Giancarlo Martino.
